g_policy.reason: The user taps Play to opt in, the offer copy states the reward (priority routing for 60 minutes), declining changes nothing, and the 'if the ad fails' field gives a path (priority turns off if the game isn't finished).

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of queue priority, which can't be withdrawn or exchanged.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app navigation event (returning to the profile menu from the Upgrade entry), not anything the user wrote.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed or capped; the proposal adds a temporary boost and normal speed stays as it is.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card sits in the profile menu drawer (s09), a sheet over the non-chat Profile screen rated safe, so it is app chrome away from any chat content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: This is an existing_anchor and the app charges for priority routing (m02, l02 'Priority routing for faster replies').

c2_evidence.reason: Claims about Janitor+ selling priority routing, the permanent Upgrade entry in the menu, and free users' normal routing (m03, inferred from s02.e07) are supported. The cost remarks are predictions, and the flow detail about returning from Upgrade is ordinary navigation.

c3_spares_payers.reason: Subscribers never see the card, per the 'subscribers' field, and the plan is not shown to remove ads. The card sits on the general profile menu, not on a paying-only screen.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is a 60-minute sample of priority routing that ends. It is not lasting access to something the app charges for, and the app already sells queue priority.

c5_moment.reason: The card sits on the profile menu, a persistent surface the user chooses to open, and it interrupts no task.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The 'if the ad fails' field says faster replies turn on when the user taps Play, so the reward is granted on a tap rather than on the verified play (REWARD_VERIFIED).

c7_specific.reason: It names the Upgrade to Janitor Plus button (s09.e31), the profile menu drawer, and the priority routing benefit (s02.e06), which are specific to this app.

other_concern: The Upgrade entry's behavior after it is tapped was not observed, so 'returning from Upgrade' as a trigger may be hard to detect. Whether the app can grant a timed priority routing state is also assumed. The reward should be granted only after REWARD_VERIFIED.
